added_lemmas.statement:
For \(\iota_{\mathrm{kill}}\), take
\[
 \mathcal G_{1/100}=\{-1/2+j/100:j=0,\ldots,250\}.
\]
There is a finite certificate \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{kill}}\) with \(K=2\), \(h=1/100\), \(U_\varepsilon=5/2\), \(b_\varepsilon=49/20\), and \(\delta_{\mathrm{enc}}=0\) such that
\[
 \operatorname{Verify}(\iota_{\mathrm{kill}},\Gamma_{\mathrm{kill}})=1.
\]
Its primal table is the globally share-uniform policy \(C(s,x)=\Theta\). Its lower-witness record \(W\) is supported at \(s^*=(2/3,1/6,1/6)\), \(A_g=1/2\), \(b=(1,1/2,1/2)\), and the two treated-multiplier vectors \(v^-_{gt}=1/2\) and \(v^+_{gt}=3\) for \((g,t)\in\mathcal D\), for which
\[
 (\theta(\eta_-),M(\eta_-))=(-1/2,13/16),\qquad
 (\theta(\eta_+),M(\eta_+))=(2,7/4).
\]
The record \(W\) stores the all-\(\Theta\) endpoint-grid profile as an integral incumbent with support-objective value \(5/2\). It also stores an explicitly indexed \(31626\)-leaf multiway branch on the zero-table interval: every proper-interval leaf carries a rational endpoint-coverage infeasibility certificate from \(\eta_-\) or \(\eta_+\), while the unique \(\Theta\) leaf carries the rational dual certificate \(r\ge7935/3200\); nonzero-table action variables are relaxed only on that last leaf, where their objective coefficients are nonnegative. Consequently,
\[
 D_{2,1/100}(\{1/100\})>\frac{7935}{3200},
 \qquad
 D_{\mathrm{det}}(1/100)>\frac{39259}{16000}>\frac{49}{20},
 \qquad
 U_\varepsilon-b_\varepsilon=\frac1{20}.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
We construct the certificate and verify each inequality used by its deterministic primal and integer lower witness.

The input is well formed under \(\mathrm{def{:}rational\text{-}certificate\text{-}input}\): \(T=3\), \(0<1/20<1/10\), \(\kappa_-=\kappa_+=1/100>0\), \(\varepsilon=1/20>0\), \(K=2\in\mathbb N_0\), and \(h=1/100>0\). The grid \(\mathcal G_{1/100}\) in the statement contains \(-1/2\) and \(2\), and every adjacent spacing equals \(1/100\).

For \(T=3\), the cohort set is \(\{2,3,\infty\}\), and the treated cells are
\[
 \mathcal D=\{(2,2),(2,3),(3,3)\}.
\tag{1}
\]
The declared least-favorable share specializes to
\[
 s^*=\left(\frac23,\frac16,\frac16\right),
\tag{2}
\]
where the coordinates are ordered as \(2,3,\infty\). Thus \(s^*\in\mathcal S_3\): every coordinate is at least \(1/6\), and their sum is one. Set
\[
 A_g=\frac12\quad(g\in\mathcal G),\qquad
 b_1=1,\quad b_2=b_3=\frac12.
\tag{3}
\]
For \(q\in\{1/2,3\}\), set \(v_{gt}=q\) on every cell in \(\mathcal D\), and call the resulting parameter \(\eta_q\). Equations (2)--(3) satisfy \(\mathrm{ass{:}observed\text{-}share\text{-}overlap}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}exposure\text{-}box}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}time\text{-}normalization}\), and \(\mathrm{ass{:}time\text{-}box}\), while both values of \(q\) satisfy \(\mathrm{ass{:}treated\text{-}multiplier\text{-}box}\).

The treated counterfactual mass \(B(\eta_q)\) is positive because (1) is nonempty and every summand \(s_gA_gb_t\) is positive. Since \(v_{gt}=q\) on every treated cell, \(\mathrm{def{:}causal\text{-}functional\text{-}setup}\) gives
\[
 H(\eta_q)=qB(\eta_q),\qquad
 \theta(\eta_q)=\frac{H(\eta_q)}{B(\eta_q)}-1=q-1.
\tag{4}
\]
Thus \(\eta_-:=\eta_{1/2}\) and \(\eta_+:=\eta_3\) have targets \(-1/2\) and \(2\), respectively. More generally, the same positive-weight identity and \(\mathrm{ass{:}treated\text{-}multiplier\text{-}box}\) show that every maintained nuisance has
\[
 \theta(\eta)=\sum_{(g,t)\in\mathcal D}
 \frac{w^0_{gt}}{B(\eta)}(v_{gt}-1)\in[-1/2,2]=\Theta,
\tag{5}
\]
because the weights are strictly positive and sum to one.

At the values in (2)--(3), the total observed mass when all treated multipliers equal \(q\) is
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 M(\eta_q)
 &=s^*_2\left(\frac12+\frac q4+\frac q4\right)
   +s^*_3\left(\frac12+\frac14+\frac q4\right)
   +s^*_{\infty}\left(\frac12+\frac14+\frac14\right).
 \end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]
Substitution of \(q=1/2\) and \(q=3\) gives, equation by equation,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 M(\eta_-)
 &=\frac23\frac34+\frac16\frac78+\frac16
 =\frac12+\frac7{48}+\frac8{48}=\frac{13}{16},\\
 M(\eta_+)
 &=\frac23\,2+\frac16\frac32+\frac16
 =\frac43+\frac14+\frac16=\frac74.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]

Under \(\mathrm{ass{:}exact\text{-}product\text{-}poisson}\), independence and multiplication of the cellwise zero probabilities imply
\[
 P_{\eta,\kappa}(X=0)
 =\prod_{g,t}\exp(-\kappa w_{gt})
 =\exp\{-\kappa M(\eta)\}.
\tag{8}
\]
For \(x>0\), direct integration gives
\[
 e^{-x}-1+x=\int_0^x(1-e^{-t})\,dt>0,
\]
and hence \(e^{-x}>1-x\). With \(\kappa=1/100\), (7)--(8) therefore yield the conservative exact rational bounds
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_{\eta_-,1/100}(X=0)
 &=e^{-13/1600}>1-\frac{13}{1600}
 =\frac{1587}{1600}>\frac{19}{20},\\
 P_{\eta_+,1/100}(X=0)
 &=e^{-7/400}>1-\frac7{400}
 =\frac{393}{400}>\frac{19}{20}.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]

Consider even the restricted honesty problem containing only these two nuisance points at the common observed share \(s^*\), and let \(I_0=C(s^*,0)\). If \(-1/2\notin I_0\), then under \(\eta_-\),
\[
 P_{\eta_-,1/100}\{-1/2\in C(s^*,X)\}
 \le 1-P_{\eta_-,1/100}(X=0)
 <\frac{13}{1600}<\frac{19}{20},
\tag{10}
\]
contradicting the required coverage \(19/20\). If \(2\notin I_0\), the same argument with \(\eta_+\) gives
\[
 P_{\eta_+,1/100}\{2\in C(s^*,X)\}
 <\frac7{400}<\frac{19}{20}.
\tag{11}
\]
Hence \(I_0\) contains both endpoints of \(\Theta\). Since every action is a connected closed subinterval of \(\Theta\),
\[
 I_0=\Theta,
 \qquad \ell(I_0)=\frac52.
\tag{12}
\]
The two-point problem is a restriction of the full maintained nuisance class: every policy honest on the full class is feasible for the two-point restrictions, so the infimum over the full feasible set is at least the infimum over the enlarged two-point feasible set. Thus every lower bound below transfers to the full problem.

We now define the lower witness as a finite, expandable verifier object. Write
\[
 I_{jk}=\left[-\frac12+\frac j{100},-\frac12+\frac k{100}\right],
 \qquad
 \mathscr J=\{(j,k)\in\mathbb Z^2:0\le j\le k\le250\}.
\tag{13}
\]
Then
\[
 |\mathscr J|=\sum_{j=0}^{250}(251-j)
 =\frac{251\cdot252}{2}=31626.
\tag{14}
\]
The finite-support integer program has binary variables \(z_{x,jk}\) for \(x\in\mathcal B_2\) and \((j,k)\in\mathscr J\), with
\[
 z_{x,jk}\in\{0,1\},
 \qquad
 \sum_{(j,k)\in\mathscr J}z_{x,jk}=1,
\tag{15}
\]
the two support-point coverage rows, and the two support-point risk rows with epigraph variable \(r\). Its root record has one child \(L_{jk}\) for each \((j,k)\in\mathscr J\), obtained by imposing \(z_{0,jk}=1\) in (15). This is an actual finite multiway branch, and the following data are stored leaf by leaf.

If \(j>0\), then \(-1/2\notin I_{jk}\). Leaf \(L_{jk}\) stores the \(\eta_-\) coverage row together with the rational enclosure in (9). Whatever actions are assigned at nonzero tables, its coverage is bounded by
\[
 1-P_{\eta_-,1/100}(X=0)<\frac{13}{1600}<\frac{19}{20}.
\tag{16}
\]
Thus the leaf's rational infeasibility certificate is the contradictory pair ``coverage at most \(13/1600\)'' and ``coverage at least \(19/20\),'' whose rational gap is
\[
 \frac{19}{20}-\frac{13}{1600}=\frac{1507}{1600}>0.
\tag{17}
\]
If \(j=0\) and \(k<250\), then \(2\notin I_{0k}\). Leaf \(L_{0k}\) instead stores the \(\eta_+\) coverage row and the rational enclosure in (9), giving
\[
 1-P_{\eta_+,1/100}(X=0)<\frac7{400}<\frac{19}{20},
 \qquad
 \frac{19}{20}-\frac7{400}=\frac{373}{400}>0.
\tag{18}
\]
Equations (16)--(18) are explicit rational endpoint-coverage infeasibility certificates for every proper-interval leaf. The only remaining leaf is \(L_{0,250}\), which fixes \(I_{0,250}=\Theta\) at zero. On that leaf, assign dual multiplier one to the \(\eta_-\) risk row, use the conservative coefficient bound \(P_{\eta_-,1/100}(X=0)\ge1587/1600\), and use only the constraints that every nonzero-table interval length is nonnegative. This rational dual certificate gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 r
 &\ge \sum_{x\in\mathcal B_2}
 P_{\eta_-,1/100}(X=x)\ell(C(s^*,x))\\
 &\ge \frac52 P_{\eta_-,1/100}(X=0)
 \ge\frac52\frac{1587}{1600}
 =\frac{7935}{3200}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{19}
\]
Concretely, the serialized leaf-certificate map in \(W\) is
\[
 \mathfrak c(j,k)=
 \begin{cases}
 \bigl(\mathsf{endpoint\text{-}minus},\,13/1600,\,19/20,\,1507/1600\bigr),
   &j>0,\\
 \bigl(\mathsf{endpoint\text{-}plus},\,7/400,\,19/20,\,373/400\bigr),
   &j=0,\ k<250,\\
 \bigl(\mathsf{risk\text{-}dual},\,1,\,1587/1600,\,5/2,\,7935/3200\bigr),
   &(j,k)=(0,250).
 \end{cases}
\tag{20}
\]
The first coordinate is a verifier tag, and every remaining coordinate is rational. The complete tree record is the finite table
\[
 \mathsf{Tree}
 =\left\{\bigl((j,k),\,z_{0,jk}=1,\,\mathfrak c(j,k)\bigr):
 (j,k)\in\mathscr J\right\}.
\tag{21}
\]
Thus expansion of (21) produces exactly \(31626\) leaf records, and (17)--(19) verify the certificate selected by each tag without an omitted leaf.

All action variables at nonzero tables may remain relaxed on \(L_{0,250}\), because their coefficients in the minimized risk and their interval lengths are nonnegative, so deleting those nonnegative contributions can only lower the objective. The root together with the indexed family \(\{L_{jk}:(j,k)\in\mathscr J\}\), the rational certificates (16)--(18), and the dual certificate (19) is therefore a complete finite branch-and-bound tree under \(\mathrm{def{:}finite\text{-}machine\text{-}certificate}\), not an unresolved root relaxation.

The record \(W\) also contains an integral incumbent, as required by that definition: set
\[
 z_{x,0,250}=1
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 z_{x,jk}=0\ \text{for }(j,k)\ne(0,250),
 \qquad x\in\mathcal B_2.
\tag{22}
\]
This is the total all-\(\Theta\) endpoint-grid profile. It has coverage one at both support points and support risk exactly \(5/2\), so \(W\) stores its support-objective value \(5/2\). Hence the witness contains both an integral incumbent and a complete lower tree.

Let \(d_W\) be the optimum of this two-support-point integer program. Every endpoint-grid policy honest over all observed shares and all maintained nuisances restricts at \(s^*\) to a feasible policy for this program, and its global worst risk is at least its worst risk over \(\{\eta_-,\eta_+\}\). Therefore \(D_{2,1/100}(\{1/100\})\ge d_W\). Equations (9) and (12) show that every feasible support profile has zero-table action \(\Theta\) and hence has risk under \(\eta_-\) strictly larger than \((5/2)(1587/1600)\). Consequently,
\[
 D_{2,1/100}(\{1/100\})\ge d_W
 >\frac52\frac{1587}{1600}
 =\frac{7935}{3200}.
\tag{23}
\]

It remains to budget count truncation and endpoint rounding. Here the union-bound Poisson mean in \(\tau_2\) is
\[
 \lambda=12\kappa_+=\frac3{25}.
\]
Let
\[
 S_5:=1-\lambda+\frac{\lambda^2}{2}-\frac{\lambda^3}{6}
       +\frac{\lambda^4}{24}-\frac{\lambda^5}{120}
 =\frac{173226647}{195312500}.
\tag{24}
\]
Repeated integration of the sixth derivative, with the first five derivatives matched at zero, gives the exact identity
\[
 e^{-\lambda}-S_5
 =\frac1{5!}\int_0^\lambda e^{-t}(\lambda-t)^5\,dt>0.
\]
Since \(1+\lambda+\lambda^2/2=1409/1250\), (24) gives the conservative exact rational tail proof
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \Pr\{\operatorname{Pois}(3/25)>2\}
 &=1-e^{-3/25}\left(1+\frac3{25}+\frac12\left(\frac3{25}\right)^2\right)\\
 &<1-\frac{173226647}{195312500}\frac{1409}{1250}
 =\frac{64279377}{244140625000}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{25}
\]
Using the definition of \(\tau_2\), (25), \(L=5/2\), and \(2h=1/50\), we obtain
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 L\tau_2+2h
 &\le \frac52\,9\Pr\{\operatorname{Pois}(3/25)>2\}+\frac1{50}\\
 &<\frac{2531639393}{97656250000}
 <\frac{13}{500};
\end{aligned}
\tag{26}
\]
the last difference is \(7423107/97656250000>0\).

For the singleton intensity range, \(\overline D_{\mathrm{det}}(\{1/100\})=D_{\mathrm{det}}(1/100)\). The lower direction of \(\mathrm{thm{:}finite\text{-}reduction}\), (23), and (26) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 D_{\mathrm{det}}(1/100)
 &\ge D_{2,1/100}(\{1/100\})-(L\tau_2+2h)\\
 &>\frac{7935}{3200}-\frac{13}{500}
 =\frac{39259}{16000}
 >\frac{39200}{16000}=\frac{49}{20}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{27}
\]

Finally, we specify the primal and the remainder of the finite machine record. Let the sole observable cell be the rational polyhedron
\[
 Q_1=\mathcal S_3\times\{1/100\},
\]
and set \(A_1(x)=\Theta\) for every \(x\in\mathcal B_2\), with the required value \(\Theta\) also used outside \(\mathcal B_2\). The nuisance cover is the single rational box \(R_1\) obtained by crossing \(Q_1\) with \(A_g\in[1/2,2]\), \(b_1=1\), \(b_t\in[1/2,2]\) for \(t>1\), and \(v_{gt}\in[1/2,3]\). By (5), the table covers the target for every point of this cell, so its coverage is exactly one and its risk is exactly \(5/2\). It is constant and therefore Borel measurable and globally uniform in the observed share.

The enclosure record \(E\) stores the rational proofs (9), (16)--(19), and (24)--(26), exact endpoint membership from (5), and exact primal coverage and risk. Every inequality used by the verifier is thus a conservative exact rational proof, not a floating-point approximation. Any unused finite-box Poisson recurrence entry is stored as the outward interval \([0,1]\) and is not invoked by any coverage, risk, infeasibility, or dual check. Consequently there is no enclosure loss beyond the explicitly proved truncation and rounding ledger, and we set
\[
 \delta_{\mathrm{enc}}=0.
\tag{28}
\]
The lower-witness record \(W\) stores the two rational support points \(\eta_-\) and \(\eta_+\), the finite integer program (15), the integral incumbent (22) with support objective \(5/2\), and the complete explicitly indexed tree (13)--(21). All tables and tree records are finite because \(|\mathcal B_2|=3^9\) and \(|\mathscr J|=31626\).

Choose
\[
 U_\varepsilon=\frac52,\qquad b_\varepsilon=\frac{49}{20},
 \qquad \delta_{\mathrm{enc}}=0.
\tag{29}
\]
The all-\(\Theta\) primal gives \(D_{\mathrm{det}}(1/100)\le U_\varepsilon\), while (27) gives \(b_\varepsilon<D_{\mathrm{det}}(1/100)\). Moreover,
\[
 U_\varepsilon-b_\varepsilon=\frac52-\frac{49}{20}=\frac1{20}=\varepsilon.
\tag{30}
\]
The rational cells cover the full declared domain, the table is total, (26) is the required outward error ledger, and \(W\) contains both the integral incumbent and the integrality-preserving complete lower tree. Therefore every clause in \(\mathrm{def{:}verifier\text{-}acceptance}\) is satisfied, so
\[
 \operatorname{Verify}(\iota_{\mathrm{kill}},\Gamma_{\mathrm{kill}})=1.
\]
added_lemmas.justification: This theorem discharges the mandatory sparse-count early-kill test with a globally share-uniform deterministic primal, a stored integral incumbent, and an explicitly indexed integrality-preserving finite lower proof.
added_lemmas.gap: The general continuum synthesis problem remains open, but this exact specialized certificate is absent from Monte Carlo finite-prior methods and qualitative drifting-subsequence asymptotics.
added_lemmas.consumer: An auditor can expand the constant finite policy table and every leaf of the finite zero-action branch tree, replay only conservative exact rational inequalities, and certify the required one-twentieth gap.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Does there exist a total synthesis algorithm which, for every exactly encoded rational \(T\), \(\alpha\), compact \(\mathcal K\), and \(\varepsilon>0\), chooses finite \(K\) and rational \(h\) and returns a finite certificate \(\Gamma\) with \(\operatorname{Verify}(\iota,\Gamma)=1\)? Every accepted output must consist of finitely many rational polyhedral observable and nuisance cells, total endpoint-grid policy tables, and outward-rounded Poisson tail and enclosure data; acceptance must imply a measurable deterministic connected-interval family honest for every \(s\in\mathcal S_T\), every \(\kappa\in\mathcal K\), and every maintained nuisance value, together with
\[
 b_\varepsilon\le\overline D_{\mathrm{det}}(\mathcal K)\le U_\varepsilon,
 \qquad 0\le U_\varepsilon-b_\varepsilon\le\varepsilon.
\]
The lower object must be a finite-support integer program accompanied by a complete exact branch-and-bound proof, not an unresolved linear relaxation. This specialized exact-certificate question is not answered by Schafer and Stark (2009): their Theorem 2 concerns Monte Carlo risk convergence, whereas their Theorem 6 gives an off-support density-ratio risk bound. Andrews, Cheng, and Guggenberger (2020), Section 2, gives qualitative drifting-subsequence criteria rather than a finite cover, computable enclosures, or a machine-checkable acceptance predicate. Because those papers use different models and action classes, no strict-strengthening or class-inclusion claim is made.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The early-kill conjunct is now discharged by thm:early-kill-certificate and must be separated from the genuinely open arbitrary-range synthesis question. The comparison is also corrected: Schafer and Stark's Monte Carlo risk-convergence statement is Theorem 2, while Theorem 6 is an off-support density-ratio bound, and the differing model and action classes do not support a strict-strengthening claim.

proposed.statement:
Does there exist a total synthesis algorithm which, for every exactly encoded rational \(T\), \(\alpha\), compact \(\mathcal K\), and \(\varepsilon>0\), chooses finite \(K\) and rational \(h\) and returns a finite certificate \(\Gamma\) with \(\operatorname{Verify}(\iota,\Gamma)=1\)? Every accepted output must consist of finitely many rational polyhedral observable and nuisance cells, total endpoint-grid policy tables, and outward-rounded Poisson tail and enclosure data; acceptance must imply a measurable deterministic connected-interval family honest for every \(s\in\mathcal S_T\), every \(\kappa\in\mathcal K\), and every maintained nuisance value, together with
\[
 b_\varepsilon\le\overline D_{\mathrm{det}}(\mathcal K)\le U_\varepsilon,
 \qquad 0\le U_\varepsilon-b_\varepsilon\le\varepsilon.
\]
The lower object must be a finite-support integer program accompanied by a complete exact branch-and-bound proof, not an unresolved linear relaxation. This specialized exact-certificate question is not answered by Schafer and Stark (2009): their Theorem 2 concerns Monte Carlo risk convergence, whereas their Theorem 6 gives an off-support density-ratio risk bound. Andrews, Cheng, and Guggenberger (2020), Section 2, gives qualitative drifting-subsequence criteria rather than a finite cover, computable enclosures, or a machine-checkable acceptance predicate. Because those papers use different models and action classes, no strict-strengthening or class-inclusion claim is made.
proposed.justification: The residual theorem-level question is whether exact fixed-design certificates can be synthesized uniformly over every observed share and every intensity in an arbitrary compact range, including zero-margin contacts.
proposed.gap: Schafer and Stark (2009), Theorem 2, proves Monte Carlo risk convergence, and their Theorem 6 gives an off-support density-ratio risk bound; neither yields a terminating continuum-honesty verifier or complete integer lower proof. Andrews, Cheng, and Guggenberger (2020), Section 2, gives qualitative drifting-subsequence criteria rather than a finite rational-polyhedral certificate.
proposed.consumer: A positive answer would let auditors synthesize and replay exact-rational sparse-count confidence certificates simultaneously over the full observed-share simplex and any declared compact intensity range.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This complete replacement removes the discharged early-kill clause and its direct dependency and free symbol, preserves only the arbitrary-range contact problem, and corrects the comparator descriptions.

proposed.comparator_claim: The estimator uses the ratio of average observed and counterfactual outcomes.
Pooled canonical-link quasi-likelihood and imputation produce identical cohort-time estimates under the stated nonlinear parallel-trends model.
Fixed-effect averages are consistent and asymptotically normal with the cross section growing and fixed \(T\).
Minimax expected-measure confidence sets are characterized using Bayes--minimax duality.
Theorem 2 gives Monte Carlo risk convergence, whereas Theorem 6 bounds off-support risk under a density-ratio condition.
The scalar Poisson interval cannot be shortened without lowering infimal coverage below its nominal level.
Auxiliary-uniform randomization splits binomial atoms and yields exact equi-tailed intervals.
An optimal interval is obtained for a single parameter in a discrete distribution under mean criteria.
Section 2 establishes uniform asymptotic size through behavior along qualitative drifting subsequences.
Explicit randomized mappings establish global asymptotic equivalence between positive Poisson and Gaussian experiments.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The earlier strict-tightening labels were unsupported across incomparable models and action classes. The table now gives the correct Schafer--Stark theorem roles and treats both it and the drifting-subsequence comparator as informing, rather than being strictly nested by, this paper.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A terminating synthesis theorem for arbitrary rational inputs and compact intensity ranges must turn the finite closed profile-validity cover into finitely many rational-polyhedral observable cells, including every zero-margin coverage and target-endpoint contact.
open_obligations.obstruction: Fixed-design exponential--polynomial separation terminates for strict rational comparisons, but at an equality contact interval refinement alone does not determine a uniformly valid side. The resulting profile-validity boundaries can be curved, and no finite rational-polyhedral refinement with one valid total table per cell has been proved.
open_obligations.attempted: Finite action-profile enumeration, compact nuisance optimization on target-membership strata, algebraic critical-component representatives, outward count-tail and endpoint error bounds, and the closed-cover Borel-selector reduction solve strict-margin and fixed-design cases. The explicit early-kill theorem now shows that neither observed-share uniformity nor integrality alone is the remaining obstacle.
open_obligations.partial_result:
For fixed \(K\) and \(h\), let \(\mathcal A\) be the finite set of complete endpoint-grid profiles and, for \(a\in\mathcal A\), define
\[
 \mathcal R_a(r)=\left\{(s,\kappa)\in\mathcal S_T\times\mathcal K:
 \inf_{\nu}q_a(s,\kappa,\nu)\ge1-\alpha,
 \quad
 \sup_{\nu}r_a(s,\kappa,\nu)\le r
 \right\}.
\]
Upper semicontinuity of coverage, continuity of risk, and compactness of the nuisance box make every \(\mathcal R_a(r)\) closed. A pointwise endpoint-grid policy of risk at most \(r\) exists exactly when
\[
 \mathcal S_T\times\mathcal K=\bigcup_{a\in\mathcal A}\mathcal R_a(r),
\]
and choosing the first valid profile gives a Borel selector. At each fixed algebraic \((s,\kappa)\), strict coverage and risk comparisons reduce to the finitely many exponential--polynomial critical components already established, and the finite-profile argument supplies an exact finite nuisance witness set for the integer optimum. Separately, \(\mathrm{thm{:}early\text{-}kill\text{-}certificate}\) constructs an accepted globally share-uniform certificate at \((T,\alpha,\kappa,K,h,\varepsilon)=(3,1/20,1/100,2,1/100,1/20)\), with \(U_\varepsilon=5/2\), \(b_\varepsilon=49/20\), and a complete integer lower tree containing an integral incumbent. The only residual question is whether the closed profile-validity cover over an arbitrary compact intensity range always admits a terminating finite rational-polyhedral refinement at zero-margin coverage and target-endpoint contacts.

prose_updates.tldr: A staggered multiplicative panel with rare Poisson totals turns the Moreau--Kastler equation (3.14) proportional-effect setup into a discrete minimax confidence problem. The contribution derives the exact low-intensity deterministic value and all optimizers, proves a strict first-order gain from randomized interval kernels, prices the stronger all-untreated-zero fallback separately, and relates both procedures to the efficient high-intensity Gaussian limit. At every fixed algebraic observed design, stratum-closure continuations reduce strict coverage and risk comparisons, including one-sided membership-switch limits, to finitely many critical-component values. The mandatory \(T=3\), \(\alpha=1/20\), \(\kappa=1/100\), \(K=2\), \(h=1/100\) test is discharged by a globally share-uniform all-\(\Theta\) primal and a complete finite integer lower tree, with a stored integral incumbent and certified gap \(1/20\). The remaining open question is total finite synthesis over arbitrary compact intensity ranges at zero-margin coverage and target-endpoint contacts.

project_justification.gap: Regular staggered-PPML work supplies the proportional target and high-information inference, while exact discrete interval work treats scalar families or finite-prior Monte Carlo approximations. Schafer and Stark (2009), Theorem 2, gives Monte Carlo risk convergence and their Theorem 6 gives an off-support density-ratio risk bound; neither it nor qualitative drifting-subsequence asymptotics converts fixed-design strict comparisons into a terminating rational-polyhedral cover valid at all exact contacts.
project_justification.niche: The proved nonregular results determine the low-intensity deterministic and randomized frontier, the separate all-untreated-zero penalty, fixed-algebraic-design strict-comparison reductions, and the high-intensity Gaussian bridge under maintained aggregate-exposure boxes and calibrated known intensity. The paper also gives an exact observed-share-uniform certificate for the mandated sparse \(T=3\) instance. Uniform finite synthesis for arbitrary compact intensity ranges remains open.
project_justification.fill: The paper joins exact low-count values and a high-count efficiency bridge to a rigorous fixed-algebraic-design reduction in which stratum-closure continuations capture attained extrema and unattained membership-switch limits. For the mandatory early-kill instance it explicitly supplies a constant all-\(\Theta\) primal, a two-point endpoint nuisance witness, a stored integral incumbent, a fully indexed multiway integer branch on the zero table, and a rational outward error ledger. The certificate format extends to general ranges, but termination over curved zero-margin contact regions remains the stated open question.

prose_updates.related_work: Moreau-Kastler (2025), equation (3.14), supplies the imputed counterfactual-share proportional target; that algebraic specialization is setup rather than a novel theorem here, and no inclusion of the present aggregate-Poisson class in theirs is claimed. Wooldridge (2023) identifies staggered nonlinear cohort-time effects and makes pooled Poisson quasi-likelihood operational under fixed \(T\), while Martin (2017), Theorems 1--2, establishes regular fixed-\(T\) asymptotics for multiplicative-panel averages; both inform the high-information endpoint. Evans, Hansen, and Stark (2005), Theorem 1, supplies Bayes--minimax duality but does not calculate this multivariate connected-interval game. Kabaila and Byrne (2001) supply the ordered scalar exact-Poisson benchmark, Kabaila (2013) supplies auxiliary-uniform atom splitting, and Habiger, McCann, and Tebbs (2013) studies integrated one-parameter discrete optimality. Bochnak, Coste, and Roy (1998) supply the semialgebraic projection, compatible-stratification, finite-component, and path facts used by the fixed-design reduction; the Poisson critical-equation cancellation and discontinuous membership-boundary treatment are derived here. Schafer and Stark (2009), Theorem 2, proves convergence of their Monte Carlo risk calculation, while Theorem 6 bounds off-support risk under a density-ratio condition. Their method does not itself provide the exact specialized early-kill certificate proved here or a terminating continuum-honesty synthesis theorem. Andrews, Cheng, and Guggenberger (2020), Section 2, gives qualitative drifting-subsequence uniformity rather than finite rational cells and machine-checkable enclosures. These comparisons concern different model and action classes, so no strict-strengthening relation is asserted. Brown, Carter, Low, and Zhang (2004), Theorems 1 and 3, informs the Poisson--Gaussian comparison, but no inclusion of the maintained aggregate-Poisson panel class in their experiment is claimed.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The fixed-design result does not claim that total coverage is one exponential--polynomial, that the discontinuous piecewise coverage function attains its extrema, or that equality contacts are decidable. It instead optimizes continuous fixed-profile extensions on compact stratum closures and includes unattained one-sided membership-switch limits; outward enclosures terminate only for strict rational comparisons. The mandated \(T=3\), \(\alpha=1/20\), \(\kappa=1/100\), \(K=2\), \(h=1/100\) instance is no longer open: the exact certificate uses the constant all-\(\Theta\) primal and a complete two-point integer lower tree with an integral incumbent. That special proof does not show that arbitrary compact intensity ranges admit a finite rational-polyhedral policy refinement across curved zero-margin contact regions, which is the sole residual certificate obstruction.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The causal-functional identity is setup credited to Moreau-Kastler (2025), equation (3.14), and the homogeneous known-mass scalar reduction is a sanity check credited to Kabaila and Byrne (2001). The independent Poisson total law and share lower bound define the experiment; the exposure, time-effect, treatment-effect, and calibrated known-intensity restrictions are maintained rather than consequences of PPML theory. The fixed-algebraic-design separation result covers strict comparisons of closure-continuation extrema and one-sided limits, not exact equality contacts or a uniform finite cover. The early-kill certificate is an exact specialization within this maintained class; it does not establish class inclusion in Moreau--Kastler (2025) or Brown, Carter, Low, and Zhang (2004), nor does it settle total synthesis over arbitrary compact ranges. An unknown or estimated intensity, noninteger outcomes, arbitrary overdispersion, individual-data sufficiency, and software-default intervals remain outside scope.

statement_notes.justification: The residual theorem-level question is whether exact fixed-design certificates can be synthesized uniformly over every observed share and every intensity in an arbitrary compact range, including zero-margin contacts.
statement_notes.gap: Schafer and Stark (2009), Theorem 2, proves Monte Carlo risk convergence, and their Theorem 6 gives an off-support density-ratio risk bound; neither yields a terminating continuum-honesty verifier or complete integer lower proof. Andrews, Cheng, and Guggenberger (2020), Section 2, gives qualitative drifting-subsequence criteria rather than a finite rational-polyhedral certificate.
statement_notes.consumer: A positive answer would let auditors synthesize and replay exact-rational sparse-count confidence certificates simultaneously over the full observed-share simplex and any declared compact intensity range.
